label: Seed 4, 8 devices, 300 s, dry. Effective representation captured AFTER Policy.__call__ applies defaults.

streamscout.side: NEITHER: it sends no cloud recall at all

rh8-demand-aware-oracle.side: CHEAP, and INJECTED; cannot run in a scored cell regardless, since it declares reads_future

refinement_to_the_prohibition.as_stated: any comparison between an arm that NAMES a representation and one that does NOT is confounded; comparisons within either group are valid.
refinement_to_the_prohibition.what_the_measurement_shows: naming against not-naming is not the right partition, because it puts simplestream (which CHOSE RECENT) in a different group from b7 (which chose nothing and was GIVEN RECENT) while both send and are charged exactly 467 tokens. They are identical at the charging path.
refinement_to_the_prohibition.proposed: partition by EFFECTIVE representation, and record separately whether it was CHOSEN or INJECTED. Effective representation is what determines comparability; chosen-against-injected is what determines whether the arm deserves credit for it.
refinement_to_the_prohibition.why_both_are_needed: an arm that chose RECENT made a decision its card can defend. An arm that named nothing received a 11.6x to 55x discount it never requested. They compare validly on cost and must not be read the same way on merit.

cascade_routing.what: it emits RICH on one query and RECENT on eight, choosing per query.
cascade_routing.status: it STRADDLES the line WITHIN ITSELF, so it cannot be assigned a side. But this is its MECHANISM, not a confound: choosing evidence by a quality-against-cost tradeoff is what cascade routing does. It is the one arm for which a mixed representation is the result rather than an artefact.
cascade_routing.constraint: it still cannot be compared cleanly against a pure-side arm, since part of any difference is the evidence discount and part is its scheduling.

streamscout.what: DEVICE on all 9 recalls, no cloud recall at all, consistent with the 9 decline rows seen at its port.
streamscout.status: outside the partition entirely. It incurs no cloud recall cost, so a cost comparison against either group measures its routing decision and nothing about representation.

second_decorative_field_found.claim_checked: that of the six fields apply_defaults injects, only `order` is injected into a field the coordinator never reads.
second_decorative_field_found.finding: NOT QUITE. The six are cadence_s, defer_s, engine_config, frame_count, order and representation. cadence_s and frame_count are read at coordinator.py:409-410, defer_s at coordinator.py:441, representation at :552 since Part A. `order` is read nowhere, and NEITHER IS `engine_config`: every occurrence under live2 is an arm WRITING it (arms.py:547, arms_builder.py:164) or a declaration. There are TWO decorative fields among the injected six, not one.
second_decorative_field_found.why_it_matters: the substance of the point stands, only representation acquired NEW semantics from Part A. But the forward-looking risk is doubled: ANY injected default into a currently-dead field is a latent copy of the representation problem, waiting for someone to give that field teeth. There are two such fields, so there are two latent instances rather than none.
second_decorative_field_found.recommendation: if engine_config is ever read, the injection must be reviewed at the same time, because every non-naming arm will silently acquire DEFAULTS["engine_config"] = "default" exactly as they acquired RECENT.

independently_confirmed.evidence: apply_defaults (interface.py:227-243) iterates action.streams, action.recall, then sets order and engine_config. It contains NO reference to action.sessions. Checked directly rather than accepted.
independently_confirmed.consequence: no arm issues offloads it did not request, so RH8 placement behaviour is its own.

measurement_scope: representation and token-side observations only. RH8 cost figures remain HELD pending the residency push; nothing in GPU-seconds is reported for any placement-acting arm.
